report:
Goal achieved in both phases.

Phase 1 (first result in ./repo): `npx swarm-verify` in ./repo. First attempt exited 4 with "incomplete: pnpm is not on PATH" — the repo pins pnpm@10.32.1 and its checks need pnpm. I installed pnpm globally (npm global prefix redirected to ~/.npm-global because /usr/local wasn't writable) and re-ran. Result: "regression-only pass" (exit 0) — 6 checks passed (build, lint, tests, placeholder, secret-scan, diff-budget), 0 failed, 4 not run with named reasons (no typecheck script; no check-only format script; no file set; no changed function to probe). Task correctness reported unmeasured (no requirement contract). Signed bundle exported under ~/.swarm/sessions.

Phase 2 (broken copy): `cp -r repo broken`, then in the copy only I flipped one assertion in tests/claude-score.test.mjs (scoreTimezone('Asia/Taipei') expected 0 → 99). Running `npx swarm-verify` in ./broken reported: "result: fail: a blocking check failed (exit 1)" — checks: 5 passed, 1 failed (tests), naming the exact failing test "upstream weights, region exceptions and risk boundaries stay intact" (187 collected, 186 passed, 1 failed). It also noted the changed file tests/claude-score.test.mjs as an observed, unauthorised change. So yes, the broken copy was correctly reported as failing.

Confusions: (1) pnpm missing and corepack enable failing with EACCES on a fresh machine — resolved by npm global prefix in home dir; (2) the tail of the pipeline masked the real exit code of the broken run in my shell (the pipeline's tail exited 0), but swarm-verify's own printed result line and exit-1 of the test command are unambiguous; (3) the repo's engines say node >=24 but the machine has Node 22.22.3 and everything ran fine.

Steps taken: ~8 run-tool commands total (inspect repo, check pnpm, corepack attempts, pnpm install deps, first swarm-verify run, pnpm global install, second swarm-verify run, copy + break + third run).
